clue.text: Prominent display to promote protective covering

blocks.note: a splash is a showy, prominent display, as in a front-page splash
to back a cause is to support or promote it

explanation.surface: A marketing plan: put on a big display to advertise some protective cover.
explanation.walkthrough: A splashback is the panel behind a sink or cooker that shields the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A splashback is a panel guarding a wall from spills, so it is a protective covering.

clue.text: Demonstration with politician stuck in traffic

indicators.note: something stuck in another thing sits wholly inside it

blocks.note: traffic as trade, buying and selling
Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A protest march with a politician caught up in a traffic jam.
explanation.walkthrough: Traffic reads as cars on the road, but here it is a noun for trading.
explanation.definitionFit: A sample shows what something is like, serving as a demonstration or specimen of the whole.

clue.text: Bowed old instrument seen around North America

indicators.note: one thing seen around another wraps it on both sides

blocks.note: the lute is an early plucked string instrument
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: An antique stringed instrument, played with a bow, turns up in North America.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowed suggests playing strings with a bow, but here it means curved; and a lute is plucked, not bowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunate means crescent-shaped, like a new moon, so curved or bowed in outline.

clue.text: A strange task in school, we recalled, on an area in Canada

indicators.note: a strange version of the words is an odd, rearranged one
the rearranged letters are placed inside the abbreviation that follows
recalled read as called back, so the word runs backwards
in a down clue, on means placed above what follows next

blocks.note: abbreviation for school
taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written before turning round
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pupils remember an odd assignment at school about a Canadian region.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas break the surface into phrases, but the wordplay ignores them; SCH is a standard abbreviation for school.
explanation.definitionFit: Saskatchewan is one of Canada's prairie provinces, a large region of the country.

clue.text: Black vessel beneath small river

indicators.note: in a down entry, something beneath comes lower, so it is written after

blocks.note: abbreviation used on pencils and in chess notation
an urn is a vase-like container

explanation.surface: A dark pot sits underneath a little stream.
explanation.walkthrough: Burn is the Scottish and northern English word for a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a burn is a stream, which is a small river.

clue.text: Some stars running wild in south Minorca

indicators.note: running wild means out of control, so the letters break their order

blocks.note: taken as written
compass abbreviation
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some film stars go wild in the south of the Balearic island of Minorca.
explanation.walkthrough: Stars hints at celebrities on holiday; it means a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Canis Minor, the Lesser Dog, is a constellation, a group of stars.

clue.text: Empire pictures is screening "The Ten Commandments"?

definitions.note: definition by example, flagged by the question mark

indicators.note: screening as concealing: the words keep the answer out of sight within them

blocks.note: the run straddles the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A cinema chain is showing the biblical film The Ten Commandments.
explanation.walkthrough: Screening looks like showing a film; it means hiding. Empire is also a well-known British cinema name.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1956 Ten Commandments is a classic Hollywood epic, a grand large-scale film.

clue.text: Python crushes extremely nourishing old animal — having no teeth

indicators.note: a python crushes prey by squeezing it in its coils, so the name surrounds the rest
extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters of the word

blocks.note: Michael Palin was one of the Monty Python team
its two end letters
common abbreviation

explanation.surface: A snake squeezes a toothless old creature that would have made a nourishing meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Python is not the snake but a member of the Monty Python comedy team, whose name does the crushing.
explanation.definitionFit: The pangolin is a scaly anteater with no teeth, eating insects with its long tongue.

clue.text: Conservative has to manage radical writer

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
to handle a matter is to manage it
abbreviation for radical

explanation.surface: A Tory is obliged to deal with an extremist author.
explanation.walkthrough: Raymond Chandler wrote the Philip Marlowe crime novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Chandler was an American novelist, a writer of hard-boiled detective fiction.

clue.text: Remote inns prepared hearty soup

indicators.note: prepared as in made ready by working ingredients together into a new form

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Isolated country pubs serve a filling soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Minestrone is a thick Italian vegetable soup with pasta, substantial enough to be called hearty.

clue.text: Article that reflects historic change in India

blocks.note: the indefinite article followed by its own mirror image, so the whole reads the same both ways

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece reflecting on a historic shift in India.
explanation.walkthrough: Change means coins, not a shift; the anna was a former Indian coin worth a sixteenth of a rupee.
explanation.definitionFit: The anna was an old Indian coin, so a piece of historic small money in India.

clue.text: Flier sides with head of physics in old boarding school

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter
the preceding letters are placed inside the school's name

blocks.note: Harrow is a long-established English public school
edges are the sides of something
its first letter

explanation.surface: A pilot takes sides with the physics master at an old boarding school.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English public school in north-west London, attended by Churchill.
explanation.definitionFit: The hedge sparrow, or dunnock, is a small bird, and any bird is a flier.

clue.text: Allow prince to be very nasty indeed

blocks.note: to let is to allow
Prince Hal, the young Henry V in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: Permitting a royal to behave terribly badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lethal can kill, which is about as harmful or nasty as a thing can be.

clue.text: A chemical weightlifters might try to get a heavenly body

blocks.note: taken as written
anabolic steroids are drugs used to build muscle

explanation.surface: Bodybuilders taking a drug in hopes of a perfect physique.
explanation.walkthrough: Heavenly body hints at the gym-built physique; it is something in space.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a rocky object orbiting the sun, so a celestial or heavenly body.

clue.text: Instrument Turner employed after lots of anguish

indicators.note: lots of the word rather than all of it, so its tail is dropped
after places the singer's name behind the other piece

blocks.note: concern is worry or anxiety
Tina Turner, the singer

explanation.surface: A musician hired after much distress.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter, but it is Tina Turner; CONCERN loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A concertina is a small bellows-driven musical instrument like a squeezebox.

clue.text: Being a landlord primarily, my inebriated clients go staggering home now?

definitions.text: Being a landlord primarily, my inebriated clients go staggering home now?

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so only the opening letters of the following words count
staggering like a drunk, lurching out of order

blocks.note: the initial letters of the two words
taken as written to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A publican watches tipsy customers lurch out at the end of the night.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: from a landlord's view, this is when drunk regulars are sent home. Being a landlord is part of that picture, not wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Closing time is the hour a pub stops serving and customers must leave.

clue.text: Term for this? Clamber possibly!

blocks.note: first meaning: a word for jumbling letters, which is what turns clamber into a near-copy of the answer
second meaning: to climb awkwardly using hands and feet

explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on itself: clamber is one letter short of a jumble of the answer, and the answer is also the name for such a jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Scramble means both to mix up or jumble and to climb hastily over rough ground, as clambering does.

clue.text: Journo's note on beer

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means sitting above what follows

blocks.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A journalist's memo about beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Journo is informal for journalist, and a reporter is a journalist who gathers news.

clue.text: Smart type takes hatchet — heartlessly heading to collect wood for fire

indicators.note: without a heart, so the central letter of the tool is removed
the heading of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a cleaver is a heavy chopping blade
its first letter
logs are burnt on a fire

explanation.surface: Someone grabs an axe and heads off to gather firewood.
explanation.walkthrough: CLEAVER drops its middle A. Clever clogs is a British informal term for a know-all.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever clogs is a person who is, or shows off being, clever, so a smart type.

clue.text: Pitman trimmed shepherd's companion

indicators.note: something trimmed has its end cut off

blocks.note: a collier is a coal miner, a man in the pit

explanation.surface: A miner with a neat haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: The collie is the classic sheepdog, the working companion of a shepherd.

clue.text: Withdraw service

blocks.note: first meaning: to retire or go somewhere
second meaning: to fix or maintain

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like cancelling a service; the formal sense of going off somewhere is easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Repair can mean to retreat to a place and also to mend, which is what servicing a machine involves.

clue.text: Attempt to arrest a physician pursuing a very old physicist

indicators.note: arresting someone means holding them, so the outer word holds the rest
pursuing means following behind, so this part comes after

blocks.note: the second a, taken as written
abbreviation
abbreviation
to have a go is to make an attempt
a plus DR, the doctor

explanation.surface: An attempt to detain a doctor who chases after an elderly scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: A DR goes inside GO, and that comes after A, V and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Amedeo Avogadro was the Italian scientist behind Avogadro's law, a physicist and chemist.

clue.text: Hoodlum's a chicken when facing term in Newgate

blocks.note: a capon is a castrated cockerel
its final letter

explanation.walkthrough: Chicken suggests a coward and term a prison sentence; both are literal here.

clue.text: Hero's vain when speaking

blocks.note: vain in the sense of futile or pointless

explanation.surface: A champion is conceited when he talks.
explanation.walkthrough: Vain suggests conceit, but it means fruitless, as in idle threats.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is someone widely admired and looked up to, as a hero is.

clue.text: Club with hot tub

blocks.note: a bat is a club used to hit a ball
H for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A golf or sports club that has a hot tub.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath is a tub filled with water for washing in.

clue.text: Fictional tale recalled in broadcast

clue.text: Some corn needed initially to make bread?

blocks.note: an ear is a head of corn
its first letter

clue.text: At first farmers say yes to grass being placed about for them?

definitions.text: At first farmers say yes to grass being placed about for them?

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of the next word
placed about means turned round to face the other way

blocks.note: its first letter
to allow something is to say yes to it
a reed is a tall grass

explanation.surface: Farmers agree to spread grass about for some animals.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: grazing deer are the ones farmers might leave grass for, with fallow also suggesting an unplanted field.
